newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Mubarak meets U.S. peace envoy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak meets U.S. peace envoy.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday discussed the future of the Middle East peace process with U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross.
The two men met in Mubarak's private residence in the Mediterranean city of Alexandria.
"Our meeting was fruitful. We discussed the peace process and the economic summit. We will continue to work and coordinate together," Ross told reporters as he was leaving Alexandria.

He was referring to a Middle East economic summit that Egypt is to host in November. Mubarak and his Foreign Minister Amr Moussa have linked the holding of the conference, which aims to integrate Israel into Middle East markets, with progress in the peace talks.
Ross argued against that Egyptian policy on Tuesday, saying: "There is no fixed timetable for making progress so there is no linkage between making progress and holding the conference."
The U.S. envoy is due in Gaza later in the day to see Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for talks on both Israeli-Palestinian talks and the results of a recent aid donors meeting.
